name: Jason Crow
page_title: Jason Crow's Issue Positions (Political Courage Test)
on_the_ballot: Running, Democratic for U.S. House (CO) - District 6

positions.question: Do you support the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade?

evidence.text: "Today we should be celebrating 51 years since Roe v. Wade established the right to an abortion. Instead, we've spent two years fighting extremists looking to enact a nationwide abortion ban. Abortion is health care. And I won't stop fighting for people's fundamental rights."
"Women deserve access to safe and effective abortion care."

"Women should have the right to make healthcare decisions that are right for them and their families. Over 70% of Americans think that women should have a legal right to an abortion. Stripping women’s health care funding from the federal budget and removing protections for women’s healthcare from our laws will hurt families across the country and in Colorado. In Congress, I have fought to protect a woman’s right to choose, while simultaneously working to continue funding critical resources like Planned Parenthood."
Rated 100% by the Planned Parenthood Action Fund

positions.question: Do you support expanding federal funding to support social safety net programs such as Social Security and Medicare?

evidence.text: "Congress must keep up with the times and expand Social Security benefits NOW."
"From protecting and strengthening Medicare and Social Security to lowering the cost of prescription drugs, I'll always keep working on behalf of older Coloradans."
Rated 100% by the National Committee to Preserve Social Security and Medicare (NCPSM

positions.question: Do you support a decrease in income taxes in order to balance the budget?

evidence.text: "Coloradans work hard. They deserve an economy that works just as hard for them. This year, I helped pass tax cuts to make it happen."
Voted in favor of HR 7024: "Tax Relief for American Families and Workers Act of 2024"

positions.question: Do you support a wealth tax in order to pay for public programs?

evidence.text: Despite exhaustive research, Vote Smart was unable to find information about this candidate's position.

positions.question: Do you support the regulation of indirect campaign contributions from corporations, unions, and individuals?

evidence.text: "Elected officials should be accountable to the people who elect them – not special interests & big corporations."

"House Republicans chose special interests and mega-donors over the American people. Our democracy is not for sale. My amendments would help put an end to corrupt influence, increase transparency, and restore public trust in government."

"Washington is broken. Too many politicians are in the pockets of the special interests that spend millions of dollars to get them elected. They stack the decks for their donors and Colorado families pay the price. We can unrig the system by ending the flood of unlimited and undisclosed money that is drowning out the voices of regular people."

"I was proud to introduce my first piece of legislation as a Member of Congress, the End Dark Money Act, to crack down on dark money in politics and close the loophole that allows mega-donors to hide their political contributions through so-called "social welfare" organizations. I also cosponsored the DISCLOSE Act, which would require organizations spending money in federal elections to disclose their donors, and the SHIELD act which requires candidates to report any offers of assistance from foreign governments to law enforcement."

positions.question: Do you support protecting government officials, including law enforcement officers, from personal liability in civil lawsuits concerning alleged misconduct?

evidence.text: "In Congress, I’ve helped bridge the trust divide between law enforcement and our community. I’ve worked to reform law enforcement training to better address the inequities facing our communities of color and I will continue this work to protect civil rights and our community."

"Today, we remember George Floyd and how the injustice of his murder echoed throughout the world. We must continue to push for accountability and transparency from law enforcement and pass the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act that was just reintroduced."
Voted in favor of HR 1280: "George Floyd Justice in Policing Act of 2021"

positions.question: Do you support increasing defense spending?

evidence.text: "While spending the largest portion of our budget on defense, our security and economic interests are increasingly dependent on negotiating a complex, competitive, and often dangerous world. Diplomacy saves American lives."

"America needs to resume its global leadership position in international institutions, and promote human rights and democracy abroad. The current administration’s foreign policy has frightened our allies, weakened our alliances, and signaled to our enemies that we are weak. Retreating from our global leadership position is not an option, and will not move the world to a safer, cleaner, and more prosperous place for our children."
"Supporting Ukraine is in the best interest of America."
Voted in favor of HR 2670: "National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024"

positions.question: Do you support federal spending as a means of promoting economic growth (e.g. grants, tax incentives)?

evidence.text: Voted in favor of HR 1319 "American Rescue Plan Act of 2021"
Voted in favor of HR 2: "Moving Forward Act"

"I fought alongside other veterans to bring the new VA hospital to Aurora and recently we helped secure a $25 million grant for infrastructure investment in Aurora. We will continue fighting to bring similar high-paying jobs to the 6th District."
Voted in favor of HR 5376 "Inflation Reduction Act of 2022"

positions.question: Do you support the federal government increasing funding for affordable housing programs?

evidence.text: "At my town hall earlier this week, over 150 Coloradans came out from across the district to talk about how we’re going to come together and find solutions to the issues facing our community, including making housing more affordable and supporting our veterans."

"Expanding housing opportunities for every Coloradan is essential. I toured Orchard Place, an apartment complex with rooms subsidized by the Englewood Housing Authority, alongside HUD’s Acting Secretary Todman and Rocky Mountain Region Administrator Jackson. We’ll continue to work together to combat the housing crisis."

"Veterans deserve to retire in dignity. Liberty View provides an affordable, multi-use housing development for veterans from all walks of life. Grateful to secure funding to create Liberty View and support Colorado’s veterans"
"We have to invest in our infrastructure today for a better tomorrow. That includes affordable housing, universal access to broadband, elder care, clean energy, clean water, and more."

positions.question: Do you support the federal government taking action, beyond those of the Federal Reserve, to alleviate inflation?

evidence.text: "Cost of living is one of the biggest issues facing Coloradan families today. That’s why I voted for the Inflation Reduction Act to lower costs of basic goods. I’ll push for more meaningful legislation to get more money in hardworking families' pockets"

"I hear every day from hardworking folks in our community who are getting squeezed by inflation & supply chain issues. Proud to vote for the #InflationReductionAct to deliver longterm relief. I look forward to the profound benefits this bill will have for the people of CO."
Voted in favor of HR 5376 "Inflation Reduction Act of 2022"
Voted in favor of HR 7688: "Consumer Fuel Price Gouging Prevention Act"

positions.question: Do you support the forgiveness of federal student loan debt?

evidence.text: "We’ve spent the last year thanking our public health care workers. But now, we need to support them by helping pay off their student loans. My bill with @RepAnnaEshoo, @michaelcburgess, & @RepGuthrie will grow & retain the public health workforce that keeps our communities safe."
Rated 100% by National Education Association

positions.question: Do you support a government-run (e.g. single-payer) healthcare program, such as Medicare-for-All?

evidence.text: "Nearly half of DACA recipients in CO don't have health insurance. Appreciate @POTUS’ work to expand access to Medicaid and #ACA coverage to Dreamers for the first time. Everyone deserves access to quality health care."

"This lawsuit would gut coverage for Coloradans w/ pre-existing conditions & jeopardize care for many CO families. Our country can’t afford a broken health care system any longer. I will continue to fight in Congress to defend + strengthen the ACA."
Voted in favor of HR 1425: "Patient Protection and Affordable Care Enhancement Act"

positions.question: Do you support expanding paid family AND/OR medical leave benefits (e.g. maternity leave)?

evidence.text: "Despite record profits during COVID, rail companies have nickel & dimed workers over just 7 days of paid sick leave. Our rail workers deserve good wages, fair treatment, & the dignity of taking paid sick leave if necessary. I voted in support of this deal & our workers."

"Not giving parents and children the time to develop and grow during those critical first weeks of life is a public health crisis — especially for families of color and working class folks in our community. It's time for #PaidLeaveForAll, and I'm all in."
Voted in favor of HR 6201 "Families First Coronavirus Response Act"

positions.question: Should the government be able to regulate the cost of prescription drugs?

evidence.text: "I’ll be going to the #StateOfTheUnion with Sue, a retired nurse & Type 1 diabetic. As drug prices skyrocket, the price of her insulin has gone up 500% forcing her to ration her medicine. This is unacceptable. The House passed the Lower Drug Costs Now Act because it’s time to act."

"Our parents & grandparents shouldn’t have to ration medication because it's unaffordable. The #InflationReductionAct caps costs & allows Medicare to negotiate drug prices. The best part? We’re paying for it by making sure big corporations start paying their fair share in taxes."
Voted in favor of HR 3 "Lower Drug Costs Now Act of 2019"
Voted in favor of HR 6833 "The Affordable Insulin Now Act"
